Triggers.value: People who look similar to the victims
When people say things like my ex

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I think about how life would have been different if the event had not occurred
become overly compliant when feeling threatened

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room

Memory.value: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words.
When I remember the event I feel intense guilt
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time

vignette: Leela is a 37-year-old South Asian woman who owns and operates a small boutique in her community. She has been married for several years and manages her business with great care and attention to detail. However, her life took a traumatic turn when she experienced a sexual assault that left deep emotional scars. The assault occurred at a local market one evening. Leela was closing up shop late into the night when an assailant broke in and forced his way through her store's back door. She recalls the intense fear as he grabbed her from behind, the smell of alcohol on his breath, and the overwhelming sense of helplessness as she struggled to escape. This event has left her with a lingering sense of vulnerability that permeates every aspect of her daily life. In the weeks following the assault, Leela began to notice specific triggers that set off vivid flashbacks and intense emotional distress. She found herself on high alert when encountering people who looked similar to those involved in the assault or hearing names reminiscent of the traumatic event. These reminders were particularly potent because they brought back the overwhelming terror she experienced during the attack. For instance, a customer at her shop who resembled one of her past acquaintances immediately triggered feelings that transported Leela back to the night of the assault. Leela also felt an acute sense of guilt when she remembered the event, believing that somehow she could have prevented it. This guilt manifested in her becoming overly compliant and submissive whenever she felt threatened. At work, this meant she often allowed unreasonable demands from customers without asserting herself, fearing confrontation or any sudden movements that might trigger a flashback. To cope with these overwhelming feelings, Leela developed several maladaptive strategies. She began to avoid using public transport altogether, opting instead for long walks home even when it meant spending hours navigating the city alone at night. This avoidance extended into her interactions with others; she was certain that any sudden movements by people around her could immediately put her on guard, making it difficult for her to feel safe in crowded or unfamiliar environments. Leela’s memory of the assault remains fragmented and nonverbal. She struggles to articulate what happened beyond vague images and sensations. This inability to fully process and verbalize her experience has left her feeling disconnected from herself and others. The terror that returned each time she recalled the event was so intense that it prevented her from discussing it with anyone, even her supportive husband. Over time, these avoidance behaviors began to take a toll on Leela’s daily life. Her business suffered as she found it increasingly difficult to manage customer interactions without feeling overwhelmed by anxiety and fear. Her marriage also felt strained; she often withdrew from social gatherings and conversations that might touch on past relationships or experiences similar to the assault. What finally brought Leela to seek help was a culmination of these mounting stressors, particularly her growing sense of isolation and despair. She had come to believe that no one could truly understand what she had gone through and feared that her life would be forever overshadowed by this trauma. In therapy sessions, she expressed the hope that she might find ways to regain control over her life and learn how to cope with the memories without feeling completely overwhelmed by them. Leela’s current state reflects a mix of intense fear and cautious optimism. She is most afraid that she will never be able to feel safe again and that the trauma will continue to dictate every aspect of her existence. However, she also holds onto hope that through therapy and support, she can begin to reclaim her sense of self and find ways to live without constant vigilance and avoidance.
